notes: Stella's option for the cartridge type is '-bs <type>' (also '-type'); '-format' selects the TV display format, not the cartridge. The 'stella' field is the name Stella lists for that type (names are case-insensitive; AUTO detects).
Gopher2600 takes '-mapping <id>' (default AUTO). The 'gopher2600' field lists the ids its cartridge loader accepts, or 'none' when it has no mapper for the format.

The 6507 sees 13 address bits, so the cartridge window is $1000-$1FFF and the same bytes appear at $3000, $5000, ... ($F000-$FFFF in the usual assembler notation). Hotspots fire on any read or write unless stated otherwise, and the access still happens on the bus.
Power-up bank is not specified by the schemes: keep the reset and interrupt vectors in every bank (or in the fixed bank for 3F, E0 and E7).
Entries with 'verified': false hold statements that two independent sources did not confirm; they are marked in 'issues' with 'Unverified'.

formats.name: Atari 2K
formats.detection: Image size 2048 bytes (Stella accepts up to 4K for its 2K type); Stella and Gopher2600 pick CV instead if the Commavid signature is present.
formats.description: 2048 bytes with no bankswitching. The cartridge only decodes A0-A10, so the image shows up twice in the 4 KB window ($F000-$F7FF and $F800-$FFFF). The CPU fetches its vectors from $FFFA-$FFFF, which are the last 6 bytes of the image.
issues: Code assembled for $F000-$F7FF and for $F800-$FFFF is the same code, so either half works for labels.
A 2K image padded to 4K should repeat the data in both halves to behave like a real 2K cart.
formats.dasm_template:
processor 6502
    include "vcs.h"
    ORG $F800
Reset
    ; ... code ...
    ORG $FFFA
    .word Reset, Reset, Reset

formats.name: Atari 8K (F8)
formats.detection: 8192-byte image. Stella tests several 8K schemes in turn (SC, E0, 3E/3F, UA, FE, 0840, E7 ...) and falls back to F8; Gopher2600 does the same through its fingerprint8k.
formats.gopher2600: F8 (also WF8 for the Coleco white-cart variant)
formats.description: Two 4 KB banks in the window $1000-$1FFF. Accessing $1FF8 selects bank 0 and $1FF9 selects bank 1, whether read or write (Horton). The vectors must be valid in both banks because the power-up bank is not guaranteed.
issues: The switch is immediate: the next instruction comes from the new bank at the same address, so the code that does the switch must exist at the same address in both banks.
Accidental accesses to $1FF8/$1FF9, for example an indexed load whose effective address lands on them, switch the bank.
Unverified: which bank is active at power-up depends on the cartridge; do not rely on it.
formats.dasm_template:
processor 6502
    include "vcs.h"
    include "macro.h"

; ---- bank 0 ----
    SEG bank0
    ORG $0000
    RORG $F000

Reset
    CLEAN_START
    ; ... code ...

    RORG $FFF0

    RORG $FFFA

    .word Reset   ; RESET
    .word Reset   ; IRQ/BRK

    RORG $F000

formats.name: Superchip (128 bytes of RAM added to 2K/4K/F8/F6/F4/EF/DF/BF)
formats.detection: Image where, in each 4K bank, the first 128 bytes equal the next 128 bytes.
formats.stella: 4KSC, F8SC, F6SC, F4SC, EFSC, DFSC, BFSC
formats.description: The Superchip adds 128 bytes of RAM at the start of the cartridge window to any of the Atari schemes. The RAM is split into a write port ($1000-$107F) and a read port ($1080-$10FF).
issues: Reading the write port writes junk into the RAM (Stella models this).

formats.name: Activision FE (8K, stack-sensed)
hotspots: Accesses to address $01FE (stack page) control the switch: JSR and RTS change banks
formats.detection: 8192-byte image with the access pattern of FE; Stella only chooses FE when the image is not F8.
formats.description: Activision scheme (Robot Tank, Decathlon) originally called SCABS, designed for up to eight 4K banks but only used with two. The cartridge watches the address bus for an access to $01FE, which happens on the stack during JSR and RTS; the bank is chosen from the top bits of the data-bus byte seen after that access, so subroutine calls and returns switch banks automatically (patent summary quoted in the Stella header).
issues: Requires the stack pointer to start at $FF so the JSR/RTS bytes land on $01FE/$01FF.
All released cartridges had only two banks.

formats.name: Parker Brothers E0 (8K, 1K slices)
formats.detection: 8192-byte image with accesses to $1FE0-$1FF7 (Stella's isProbablyE0).
formats.description: Parker Brothers scheme. The 4 KB window is four 1 KB slots. Slot 0 ($1000-$13FF) takes any 1 KB slice of the 8K ROM by accessing $1FE0-$1FE7, slot 1 by accessing $1FE8-$1FEF and slot 2 by accessing $1FF0-$1FF7; slot 3 ($1C00-$1FFF) always shows the last 1 KB.
issues: The vectors and start-up code must be in the fixed last 1 KB.
Horton's text gives the third range as $1FF0-$1FF8; Stella's header and Gopher2600 use $1FF0-$1FF7 (eight slices).

formats.name: M-Network E7 (16K + 2K RAM)
hotspots: $1FE8-$1FEB select the 256-byte RAM block shown at $1800-$19FF
formats.ram: 2 KB in two parts: 1 KB at $1000-$17FF when $1FE7 was accessed (write port $1000-$13FF, read port $1400-$17FF), plus four 256-byte blocks shown at $1800-$19FF (write port $1800-$18FF, read port $1900-$19FF)
formats.detection: Image of 8K to 16K whose code accesses the $1FE0-$1FEB hotspots (Stella isProbablyE7/E78K, Gopher2600 fingerprintMnetwork).
formats.description: M-Network scheme. The 4 KB window is two 2 KB halves. The upper half ($1800-$1FFF) always shows the last 2 KB of the ROM. The lower half shows one of seven 2 KB banks, selected by accessing $1FE0-$1FE6; accessing $1FE7 puts 1 KB of RAM there instead. The first 512 bytes of the upper half become one of four 256-byte RAM blocks (selected with $1FE8-$1FEB) with separate write and read ports.
issues: Horton's text lists $1FF8-$1FFB for the 256-byte block select; Stella and Gopher2600 both use $1FE8-$1FEB, which is what is recorded here.
Only one commercial cartridge used the RAM.
Stella handles 8K images with hotspots $1FE4-$1FE7 and 12K images with $1FE0-$1FE7 (smaller bank counts).

formats.name: Tigervision 3F (up to 512K, 2K banks)
hotspots: Write of the bank number to $3F (any write to $00-$3F)
formats.detection: Images containing STA $3F style writes (Stella isProbably3F, Gopher2600 fingerprint3f); for 8K images Stella checks for it after SC/E0/3E.
formats.description: Tigervision scheme. The window is two 2 KB halves: the upper half ($1800-$1FFF) always shows the last 2 KB of the ROM and the lower half shows the 2 KB bank whose number is written to $3F. In fact any write to $00-$3F changes the bank, so use $40-$7F for TIA writes that must not switch banks. The scheme supports up to 512 KB.
issues: Writes to TIA registers at $00-$3F also switch the bank; use the mirror at $40-$7F.
The last 2 KB bank must hold the vectors.
formats.dasm_template:
processor 6502
    include "vcs.h"
    ; bank k selected with: lda #k : sta $3F   (writes to $3F)
    ORG $0000 : RORG $F000   ; bank 0 (2K)
    ; ... switchable 2K
    ; last bank placed at $F800
    ORG $07FA : RORG $FFFA
    .word Reset, Reset, Reset

formats.name: Tigervision 3E (3F + RAM)
formats.size: up to 512K ROM + up to 32K RAM
hotspots: Write bank number to $3F: map ROM bank
Write bank number to $3E: map RAM bank
formats.ram: up to 32 RAM banks of 1 KB; when a RAM bank is selected the lower 2K half shows it twice: read port $1000-$13FF and write port $1400-$17FF
formats.detection: Image containing STA $3E, LDA #imm (Stella and Gopher2600 search for that pattern).
formats.description: Tigervision 3F plus RAM. The lower 2 KB half shows either a 2 KB ROM bank (number written to $3F) or a 1 KB RAM bank (number written to $3E); the upper 2 KB half is fixed to the last ROM bank. Stella numbers RAM banks after the ROM banks.
issues: Only 240 ROM banks are supposed to be used for compatibility with some flash carts (Stella header).
Stella gives every game all 32 KB of RAM because the real RAM size is not known.

formats.name: Tigervision 3E+ (segmented ROM/RAM)
hotspots: Write to $3F: bits 7-6 = slot, bits 5-0 = 1 KB ROM bank
Write to $3E: bits 7-6 = slot, bits 5-0 = 512-byte RAM bank
formats.ram: up to 64 banks of 512 bytes; a RAM bank is read at the start of its 1K slot and written 512 bytes higher (for example read $1000-$11FF, write $1200-$13FF)
formats.detection: Image containing the ASCII text 'TJ3E' (both emulators).
formats.description: Modified 3E ('TJ' version in Stella's list) made for a 'Boulder Dash' style tiling engine: the window is four 1 KB slots ($1000, $1400, $1800, $1C00). A write to $3F maps a 1 KB ROM bank into a slot; a write to $3E maps a 512-byte RAM bank. The top two bits of the value select the slot (0-3), the low six bits the bank (0-63).
issues: Unlike 3E, the last slot is not fixed: it starts on the FIRST 1 KB of the ROM, so the vectors must be at the end of the first 1 KB of the image.
The 3E+ limits (64K ROM, 32K RAM) are much lower than 3E's.

formats.name: CBS RAM Plus (FA)
formats.detection: 12288-byte image (both emulators choose FA from the size alone).
formats.description: CBS RAM Plus. Three 4 KB banks selected by accessing $1FF8-$1FFA, plus 256 bytes of RAM with separate write and read ports.
issues: Stella's source comment says bit D0 of the written value must be 1, but the code that acts on the hotspots has that test commented out, so any access switches the bank.
Used by CBS games such as Tunnel Runner and Omega Race.
formats.dasm_template:
processor 6502
    include "vcs.h"
    include "macro.h"

; ---- bank 0 ----
    SEG bank0
    ORG $0000
    RORG $F000

Reset
    CLEAN_START
    ; ... code ...

    ORG $0FF0
    RORG $FFF0
    ; bankswitch trampoline: must live at the same address in every bank
    ; to switch to bank k: lda $FFF8+k (read) or sta (write), then continue from the same address
    ORG $0FFA
    RORG $FFFA
    .word Reset   ; NMI
    .word Reset   ; RESET
    .word Reset   ; IRQ/BRK

; ---- bank 1 ----
    SEG bank1
    ORG $1000
    RORG $F000

    ; bank 1 code (each bank needs its own copy of the code that runs while switching)

    ORG $1FF0
    RORG $FFF0
    ; bankswitch trampoline: must live at the same address in every bank
    ; to switch to bank k: lda $FFF8+k (read) or sta (write), then continue from the same address
    ORG $1FFA
    RORG $FFFA
    .word Reset   ; NMI
    .word Reset   ; RESET
    .word Reset   ; IRQ/BRK

; ---- bank 2 ----
    SEG bank2
    ORG $2000
    RORG $F000

    ; bank 2 code (each bank needs its own copy of the code that runs while switching)

    ORG $2FF0
    RORG $FFF0
    ; bankswitch trampoline: must live at the same address in every bank
    ; to switch to bank k: lda $FFF8+k (read) or sta (write), then continue from the same address
    ORG $2FFA
    RORG $FFFA
    .word Reset   ; NMI
    .word Reset   ; RESET
    .word Reset   ; IRQ/BRK

formats.name: FA2 (CBS RAM Plus 28K/32K)
formats.detection: Stella: 24K or 28K-32K images through isProbablyFA2/ARM; Gopher2600 fingerprintFA2.
formats.description: Extension of FA for the Harmony cartridge: six or seven 4 KB banks selected by accessing $1FF5-$1FFA (or $1FFB), and the 256-byte RAM can be saved to or loaded from the Harmony's flash by accessing $1FF4. In 29K images the first 1K is ARM driver code, which an emulator ignores.
issues: Unverified: exact bank count per image variant.

formats.name: Dynacom Megaboy F0 (64K)
formats.detection: 64K image after the 3E/3F/4A50/EF/X07 tests fail.
formats.description: Dynacom Megaboy. 16 banks of 4 KB. Accessing $1FF0 advances to the next bank, wrapping from 15 to 0, so banks can only be reached in sequence; the game stores the current bank number at $1FEC (Horton) and loops until it matches.
issues: Only the Megaboy cart is known to use it.

formats.name: UA Limited (8K)
formats.detection: 8192-byte image with accesses to the $0220/$0240 hotspots (Stella isProbablyUA).
formats.description: UA Limited scheme. Two 4 KB banks switched by accessing addresses below $1000, outside the cartridge window: $0220 selects bank 0 and $0240 selects bank 1. Brazilian licensed hardware used shifted addresses ($02A0 and $02C0), which Stella also accepts. Known titles: Funky Fish, Pleiades.
issues: The hotspots fall in TIA/RIOT mirror space, so the access also happens on the TIA bus.
Some dumps have the banks in reverse order; use UASW for those.

formats.name: EconoBanking (0840)
formats.detection: 8192-byte image with accesses to $0800/$0840 (Stella isProbably0840).
formats.description: EconoBanking. Two 4 KB banks selected by accessing $0800 (bank 0) or $0840 (bank 1), outside the cartridge window; any read or write fires.
issues: The hotspot addresses are in the TIA mirror area, so the access also reaches the TIA.

formats.name: X07 (AtariAge 64K)
hotspots: Address pattern 0 1xxx nnnn 1101: select bank nnnn
Address pattern 0 0xxx 0nxx xxxx: banks 14/15 select bit n
formats.detection: 64K image with X07 hotspot accesses (Stella isProbablyX07).
formats.description: Scheme by John Payson and Fred Quimby: 16 banks of 4 KB with hotspots below $1000. Two patterns are used: an address of the form 0 1xxx nnnn 1101 selects bank nnnn; an address of the form 0 0xxx 0nxx xxxx switches between banks 14 and 15 (bank 111n) only when the current bank is already 14 or 15.
issues: Stella notes the second pattern hits on almost any TIA access.

formats.name: Pitfall II DPC
formats.ram: 2 KB display data inside the DPC chip, read through the data fetchers
formats.detection: Image of 10240 bytes (also 10495/10496 in Gopher2600; Stella accepts 10-11K).
formats.description: Pitfall II. Two 4K program banks switched like F8 (hotspots $1FF8 and $1FF9), a 2 KB display ROM and the DPC chip (patent US 4,644,495). The chip registers are at $1000-$107F: $1000-$103F is the read port and $1040-$107F the write port.
issues: The chip also supplies the music generator and random numbers; emulators implement it in the mapper.

formats.name: DPC+ (Harmony/Melody)
formats.ram: Harmony 8K RAM: 3K ARM driver, 4K display data, 1K frequency tables
formats.detection: The string 'DPC+' occurs at least twice in the image (both emulators).
formats.description: Enhanced DPC for Harmony/Melody. The first 3K of the 32K image is the ARM driver, six 4K banks hold the 6502 code, bankswitching uses $1FF6-$1FFB, and the DPC registers are at $1000-$107F (read $1000-$103F, write $1040-$107F). Eight data fetchers, three music channels and a 32-bit random generator; an optional fast-fetch mode.
issues: Needs the matching ARM driver in the image; plain 6502 emulation is not enough.

formats.name: CDF / CDFJ (Harmony/Melody, ARM)
hotspots: $1FF0-$1FF3: data-stream and mode registers (Gopher2600 names DSWRITE, DSPTR, SETMODE, CALLFN)
formats.ram: 8K: 4K display data plus 4K for ARM variables and stack
formats.detection: Stella: 'CDF' appears 3 times in the image, or the string 'PLUSCDFJ'. Gopher2600: 'CDFJ' within the first 2048 bytes (CDFJ), 'PLUSCDFJ' (CDFJ+), or the old 'CDFx' version bytes repeated twice.
formats.gopher2600: CDF, CDF0, CDF1, CDFJ (aliases: CDF selects the CDFJ layout)
formats.description: Chris, Darrell, Fred (and John) scheme: seven 4K banks, 32 fast fetchers, two jump queues, a parameter queue and sampled audio. Bankswitching uses $1FF5-$1FFB; the start bank is bank 6.
issues: The ARM driver differs between CDF0, CDF1 and CDFJ; Gopher2600 has one mapping id per version, Stella has a single 'CDF' type.

formats.name: CDFJ+ (larger ROM and RAM)
formats.detection: String 'PLUSCDFJ' in the image (both emulators).
formats.description: CDFJ extended for the LPC213x family: ROM sizes 64/128/256/512K and RAM 16/32K. Bankswitching uses $1FF4-$1FFA and the start bank is 0.
issues: The programmer must stay within the RAM and ROM of the target device (Stella header).

formats.name: BUS (BusStuffing / Harmony cart)
formats.ram: ARM-managed RAM: 4K display data, 1K ARM variables and stack
formats.detection: The string 'BUS' occurs at least twice in a 32K image (Stella).
formats.description: 'Bus stuffing' for Harmony-class carts by Darrell Spice Jr, Chris Walton, Fred Quimby and others. The ARM binary is the first 4K of the 32K image; the 6502 talks to it through registers at $1000-$103F (communication stream at $1010, jump stream at $1011), and the ARM can drive the data bus on precisely timed cycles so the 6502 executes instructions the ARM synthesises.
issues: Unverified: Stella's header speaks of seven 4K program banks while its code handles six hotspots ($1FF6-$1FFB); treat the bank layout as uncertain.
Stella marks the scheme experimental and may remove it.

formats.name: ELF (relocatable ARM ELF: PlusCart, Chameleon, UnoCart)
formats.ram: ARM RAM sections, supplied by the loader
formats.detection: Stella: ELF magic 7F 'E' 'L' 'F', little-endian, type ET_REL and ARM machine. Gopher2600: ELF magic at the start of the file.
formats.gopher2600: ELF (ELF_in_ACE for an ELF wrapped in ACE)
formats.description: The game is a relocatable 32-bit little-endian ARM ELF object that the cartridge firmware (or the emulator) links and loads. The ARM code uses vcsLib stubs (vcsWrite3, vcsSta3, vcsJmp3, vcsNop2, vcsLda2, vcsLdaForBusStuff2, vcsLdxForBusStuff2, vcsLdyForBusStuff2, vcsWaitForAddress, vcsStartOverblank, vcsEndOverblank, vcsCopyOverblankToRiotRam and others) that queue bus transactions replayed on exact 6507 cycles; the 6507 therefore runs code that the ARM generates. There is no fixed bank layout or hotspot.
issues: Stella's ELF core is by Christian Speckner; Gopher2600's mapper lists the vcsLib names above.
Unverified (project experience, not in the sources used): PlusCart firmware 2.3.32 loads full games but may lack some vcsLib symbols, and older Gopher2600 builds abort on code in RAM (.RamFunc).
Unverified: Chameleon Cart sizes (about 36 KB RAM, 128 KB flash on the G070 version) come from the project's own notes, not from vendor documentation.

formats.name: Supercharger (AR)
formats.size: 8448 bytes per load (multi-load images are multiples)
hotspots: $1FF8 configuration byte (bank pair, write enable, ROM power)
$1850 load trigger when the BIOS ROM is mapped in the upper window (Stella)
formats.ram: 6K of RAM in three 2K banks, plus 2K BIOS ROM
formats.detection: Stella: image size 6K-33K; Gopher2600: size is a multiple of 8448 bytes (or a sound/tape image).
formats.description: Starpath Supercharger: 6K RAM loaded from tape (audio) in 8448-byte loads, each 8192 bytes of data plus a 256-byte header, and a 2K BIOS ROM. The upper and lower 2K windows of the cartridge area are mapped independently by a configuration byte written to $1FF8 (bits 4-2 select the bank pair, bit 1 enables RAM writes, bit 0 powers the ROM). RAM writes use an unusual address-bus protocol: a held byte is committed on an access exactly five bus cycles after the arming access.
issues: Needs a BIOS (emulators stub it); not a format for new development.

formats.name: EF (64K)
formats.detection: 64K image with accesses to $1FE0-$1FEF (Stella isProbablyEF).
formats.stella: EF (EFSC with 128 bytes of RAM, EFF variant)
formats.description: Scheme from the Homestar Runner cartridge by Paul Slocum: sixteen 4 KB banks, selected by accessing any address in $1FE0-$1FEF; the low 4 bits of the address are the bank number. DF and BF extend it.
issues: In EFSC the 128-byte Superchip RAM sits at $1000-$10FF as in other SC types.

formats.name: DF (128K)
formats.detection: 128K image with accesses to $1FC0-$1FDF (Stella isProbablyDF).
formats.description: CPUWIZ extension of EF to 32 banks: accessing $1FC0-$1FDF selects the bank whose number is the low 5 bits of the address.
issues: Gopher2600 has no separate DFSC id (its DF mapper handles it).

formats.name: SB (128K-256K)
hotspots: $0800-$081F (128K) or $0800-$083F (256K): address bits give the bank
formats.detection: 128K or 256K image (the fallback after CDF/3E/3F/4A50 checks in Stella; Gopher2600 fingerprintSB).
formats.description: SUPERbanking. The bank is chosen by the address of an access in the lower address space: $0800-$081F selects one of 32 banks (128K) and $0800-$083F one of 64 banks (256K); the low bits of the address are the bank number. The hotspot block mirrors at $0900, $0A00 ... up to $0FFF.
issues: The hotspots fall in TIA/RIOT mirror space, so the access reaches the TIA bus too.

formats.name: 4A50 (64K)
hotspots: Many address-bus patterns in $1Exx/$1Fxx (see the Stella page)
formats.ram: RAM and ROM slices mixed (see description)
formats.detection: 64K image (Stella isProbably4A50 looks at the reset vector layout).
formats.description: Scheme by John Payson (documented at stella-emu.github.io/4A50.html). The window has four parts: a 2K slice that can show any 2K of RAM or of the first 32K of ROM, a 1.5K slice for any 1.5K of RAM or of the last 32K of ROM, a 256-byte slice for any 256-byte page of RAM or ROM, and a last 256 bytes fixed to the end of the ROM.
issues: Stella states the scheme is not fully implemented (hires helpers and a page-wrap case are missing).
Unverified: exact hotspot addresses; the 4A50 page was not opened in this pass.

formats.name: BF (CPUWIZ 256K)
formats.description: Extension of EF/DF to 64 banks of 4 KB: accessing $1F80-$1FBF selects the bank whose number is the low 6 bits of the address. The BFSC variant adds the 128-byte Superchip RAM.
formats.detection: 256K image with accesses to $1F80-$1FBF (Stella isProbablyBF).

formats.name: CV (Commavid extra RAM)
formats.description: Commavid scheme: 2 KB of ROM at $1800-$1FFF and 1 KB of RAM in the lower half of the window, with a read port at $1000-$13FF and a write port at $1400-$17FF. There is no bankswitching.
formats.detection: 2K or 4K image that Stella/Gopher2600 recognise by the Commavid signature (isProbablyCV / fingerprintCV).
issues: Titles using it include Jawbreaker and Rescue Terra I (Stella header).
